a49_tail: in one dimension the matching background needs a rule of unlimited reach (a comparison).
a51_bullet: - **Farther-reaching rules (A51, under your decision 22; its exact side result checked by me).** We let the rule reach as far as the grid allows and searched backwards again. Longer reach lowers the background's leftover restlessness only through very long, smooth links that check how evenly spin is spread over the whole grid, which nearly any quiet state passes; slightly magnet-like states gain as much or more, and on the largest grid (1,000 places) one does better. With those links set aside, the restlessness stays the same however far the rule reaches and however big the grid. Steadiness alone is cheap: a pattern of locked pairs is exactly steady under a short rule (exact; checked). Under its own best rule the background does beat every rival tried, by clear margins on grids of 216, 512 and 1,000 places, and that rule is extremely frustrated (no single ordered pattern is favoured). But on a 16-place grid, where the calmest state can be found exactly, it sits far below the background. Whether that also holds on larger grids is open.
